primitives.name: Linearized Pythagorean
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model - Analytic proof: first-order multivariate Taylor expansion of f(x,y) = x^γ/(x^γ + y^γ) about (R_avg, R_avg), yielding WP ≈ 0.500 + [γ/(4R_avg)](RS - RA).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'WP': 'dimensionless winning percentage in [0,1]', 'RS': 'dimensionless runs scored', 'RA': 'dimensionless runs allowed', 'R_avg': 'league average runs per team-season', 'γ': 'dimensionless exponent parameter'}
primitives.assumptions: Runs scored and allowed follow power-law scaling; league average is constant; first-order Taylor expansion valid near (R_avg, R_avg).
primitives.breakdown_regime: When RS or RA deviates significantly from R_avg, or when γ varies substantially across leagues.

layer2.mapping: Used in GSE for point-differential-based win probability projections; in GSI for Bayesian win-rate inference with uncertainty quantification.
layer2.telemetry: Per-season R2 of OLS fit and confidence interval coverage of γ̂.

primitives.name: Run Differential Coefficient
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'β': 'win percentage change per unit run differential', 'γ': 'dimensionless exponent parameter', 'R_avg': 'league average runs per team-season'}
primitives.assumptions: Local linearity around equilibrium point (R_avg, R_avg); constant league average.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When league scoring dynamics shift or when β becomes unstable due to extreme R_avg values.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to NFL point-differential models via re-fitting γ̂_NFL; used in GSE for quick expected-win conversions.
layer2.telemetry: Per-season β̂ estimates and their consistency with Jones & Tappin baseline.

primitives.name: Pythagorean Exponent Estimation
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Empirical: OLS of WP on (RS - RA) per season with intercept constrained/estimated at α = 0.500; per-season γ̂ recovered via γ̂ = β̂·4·R_avg; 95% CIs on γ̂ with Bonferroni correction (α = 0.05/20 = 0.0025).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'γ̂': 'estimated Pythagorean exponent', 'β̂': 'estimated linear coefficient', 'R_avg': 'league average runs per team-season'}
primitives.assumptions: OLS regression holds; Bonferroni correction ensures multiple-test validity; β̂ derived from linear fit.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When OLS fails due to collinearity or non-normality of residuals; when γ̂ exceeds empirical bounds.

layer2.mapping: Used in GSE to validate NFL-specific γ̂_NFL against accepted values (~2.37); in GSI for robustness checks on exponent estimates.
layer2.telemetry: Coverage of 95% CI for γ̂ and agreement with Miller (2007) γ ≈ 1.82.

The core derivation begins with the nonlinear Pythagorean formula WP = RS^γ / (RS^γ + RA^γ). A first-order Taylor expansion about the equilibrium point (R_avg, R_avg) yields a linear approximation: WP ≈ 0.5 + γ/(4R_avg)(RS - RA). This establishes a direct relationship between run differential and winning percentage. The partial derivatives ∂f/∂x = γ/(4·R_avg) and ∂f/∂y = -γ/(4·R_avg) confirm that the slope is symmetric and depends on γ and R_avg. The empirical estimation of γ̂ via β̂ = γ̂/(4·R_avg) allows for retroactive fitting of the exponent. The method assumes local linearity and stable league averages, which may fail under extreme scoring environments or when γ varies significantly across eras or sports. The dual nature of the model—both analytical and empirical—enables robust validation through OLS regression and confidence intervals.
